panels.description: The p50, p95 and p99 of the duration of the successful calls (status ok) of the selected job, command and sub-command, over a window of $__rate_interval, at least 1 h (Min step 15m). With All, the quantiles are of all the calls together. Metric: devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds. A run of a command group with no sub-command, such as devops ci, sends no point to this histogram (#5192).
panels.title: Latency: p50, p95 and p99 of successful calls

panels.description: The calls of the selected job, command and sub-command in each hour, ok and error together. Each bar is the hour before its time (Min interval 1h). Metric: histogram_count of devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds. A run of a command group with no sub-command, such as devops ci, sends no point to this histogram (#5192). Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: Traffic: calls per hour

panels.description: The share of the calls of the selected job, command and sub-command that ended with the status error, over a window of $__rate_interval, at least 1 h (Min step 15m). A selection with calls and no error shows 0. Metric: devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds. A run of a command group with no sub-command, such as devops ci, sends no point to this histogram (#5192).
panels.title: Errors: share of calls that failed

panels.description: The GitHub requests of the roadmap Service in the last hour, as a share of its hourly budget service.github_requests_per_hour. The dashed line is the limit, 100 %. Only the Service keeps this budget: the cluster Jobs and the workstations do not count in it. Metrics: devops_cli_service_budget_spent_requests and devops_cli_service_budget_limit_requests. The panel shows the Service budget until #4752 records the rate limit of each GitHub answer.
panels.title: Saturation: share of the Service GitHub budget used

panels.description: The calls of each command in the time range, from the most calls down. Each run of devops counts once, also a run of a command group with no sub-command, such as devops ci, so a command can show more calls here than in the sub-command table. Metric: devops_cli_command_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: Traffic: calls of each command in the range

panels.description: For each command in the time range: the calls, the calls that ended in an error, the error share, and the p50, p95 and p99 of the duration of all the calls. The command histogram has no status, so its quantiles include the failed calls. The rows are sorted by errors, then by calls. Click a command to show its golden signals at the top of the dashboard. Metrics: devops_cli_command_total and devops_cli_command_duration_seconds. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a share or a quantile can come out high or low.

targets.expr: (sum by (command) (increase(devops_cli_command_total{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",status="error"}[$__range])) or sum by (command) (increase(devops_cli_command_total{job=~"$job",command=~"$command"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (command) (increase(devops_cli_command_total{job=~"$job",command=~"$command"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Commands: calls, errors and latency in the range

panels.description: The log records of devops-cli in Loki at the level error, critical or fatal (detected_level), newest first, with the trace identifier linked to Tempo. Warnings are not shown.
panels.title: Errors: error logs of devops-cli

panels.description: For each sub-command of the selected job, commands and sub-commands in the time range: the calls, the calls that ended with the status error, the error share, and the p50, p95 and p99 of the duration of the successful calls. The rows are sorted by errors, then by calls. Click a sub-command to show its golden signals at the top of the dashboard. The sub-commands come from the series, so a new sub-command shows with no change to the dashboard. Metric: devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a share or a quantile can come out high or low.

targets.expr: round(histogram_count(sum by (command, sub_command) (increase(devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",sub_command=~"$sub_command",status="error"}[$__range]))) or histogram_count(sum by (command, sub_command) (increase(devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",sub_command=~"$sub_command"}[$__range]))) * 0)

(histogram_count(sum by (command, sub_command) (increase(devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",sub_command=~"$sub_command",status="error"}[$__range]))) or histogram_count(sum by (command, sub_command) (increase(devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",sub_command=~"$sub_command"}[$__range]))) * 0) / histogram_count(sum by (command, sub_command) (increase(devops_cli_subcommand_duration_seconds{job=~"$job",command=~"$command",sub_command=~"$sub_command"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Sub-commands: calls, errors and latency in the range

panels.description: For each stage of a RAG query in the time range: the queries, and the p50, p95 and mean of the duration. total is the whole query, from embedding the query to the ranked results. embedding is the query embedding through the gateway. search is the Qdrant searches, which run at once, so the stage takes as long as the slower search. ranking is the local ranking of the results. Each quantile is its own, so the stages need not add up to total. Queries sent before #975 carry no stage and are left out. Metric: devops_cli_rag_query_duration_ms. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a share or a quantile can come out high or low.
panels.title: Latency: RAG query stages in the range

panels.description: Qdrant requests retried in the time range after a transient error, by client operation and error type, from the most down. The error type is the class of the error behind the retry, taken from inside the ResponseHandlingException the Qdrant client wraps transport errors in: RemoteProtocolError for a keep-alive connection the tunnel closed while idle, ConnectError for a refused connection, ReadTimeout for a request that waited out qdrant.timeout, 300 s by default. Each retry reconnects after a pause of 0.5 s times the attempt number, which a search spends in the search stage. Metric: devops_cli_qdrant_retries_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: Errors: Qdrant retries in the range

panels.description: The share of the embedding cache lookups that a cache answered, from the memory cache of the process or from Valkey, over a window of $__rate_interval, at least 1 h (Min step 15m). A window with lookups and no hits shows 0. Each text that an embedding request gets is one lookup. Metric: devops_cli_embedding_cache_lookups_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a share or a quantile can come out high or low.
panels.title: Cache: share of embedding lookups that hit

panels.description: For each target type of a review (branch, pr or path) in the time range: the reviews, and the p50, p95 and mean of the review duration. Metric: devops_cli_review_duration_seconds. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a share or a quantile can come out high or low.
panels.title: Latency: AI reviews by target type in the range

panels.description: Review findings in the time range, by severity (the label severity), from the most down. Metric: devops_cli_findings_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low. `review pr --post --no-reporting` records no findings metric, so those runs are missing (#791).
panels.title: Findings: count by severity in the range

panels.description: Review findings in the time range, by persona (the label producer), from the most down. Metric: devops_cli_findings_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low. `review pr --post --no-reporting` records no findings metric, so those runs are missing (#791).
panels.title: Findings: count by persona in the range

panels.description: Review findings in the time range, by status (the label status), from the most down. Metric: devops_cli_findings_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low. `review pr --post --no-reporting` records no findings metric, so those runs are missing (#791).
panels.title: Findings: count by status in the range

panels.description: LLM spend over the dashboard's time range. Approximate, and low for sparse series: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, so a series' first sample, and any series seen only once in the window, add nothing. Delta points from one process can arrive out of order, and totals then come out low (#792).
panels.title: AI Spend in Range

panels.description: The GitHub core requests in each hour that cost quota, by job, beside the answers 304 that cost no quota (free (304)) and the hourly budget of the Service (Service budget limit, dashed). Only the requests of roadmap-service count in this budget. A stage Job (job roadmap-stage) counts its requests in a budget of its own, roadmap.stage.github_requests_per_hour (#4559). The Service and the cluster Jobs act as one GitHub App and share the rate limit of its installation, and a workstation (job devops-cli) uses the token of its person. Each attempt counts, and each retry counts again. Each bar is the hour before its time (Min interval 1h). Metric: devops_cli_github_requests_total, resource core. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: GitHub quota: core requests per hour

panels.description: The GitHub requests in each hour that cost quota, for the rate-limit resources other than core: graphql, search, and Other for each other resource, such as code_search and dependency_sbom. Each bar is the hour before its time (Min interval 1h). Metric: devops_cli_github_requests_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: GitHub quota: requests of the other resources per hour

panels.description: The GitHub requests in the time range that GitHub refused with a rate limit, or that got a 5xx for a read of the GitHub session, and that devops-cli sent again after a wait. A range with no throttle shows 0. Metric: histogram_count of devops_cli_github_throttle_wait_seconds. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: Throttles: count in the range

panels.description: For each rate-limit resource in the time range: the throttles, and the seconds that devops-cli waited before it sent a refused request again. Metric: devops_cli_github_throttle_wait_seconds. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: Throttles: count and wait by resource in the range

panels.description: The GraphQL points in each hour that GitHub reported in the rateLimit field of each answer, by job, beside the hourly limit of a token, 5,000 points (dashed). A GitHub App installation can have a higher limit. One query can cost many points, so the count of graphql requests does not show this cost. Each bar is the hour before its time (Min interval 1h). Metric: devops_cli_github_graphql_points_total. Approximate: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, and delta points from one process can arrive out of order (#792), so a count can come out low.
panels.title: GitHub quota: GraphQL points per hour

panels.description: Tool calls of the stage planner in the last hour, by tool and outcome (ok, empty or error), on the left axis, and the mean size of the answers of each tool in characters, after the cut of the tool, on the right axis. The planner runs in the stage Jobs, whose series have the job roadmap-stage (#4559). Approximate, and low for sparse series: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, so a series' first sample, and any series seen only once in the window, add nothing. Delta points from one process can arrive out of order, and totals then come out low (#792). A tool that no run calls shows a line at 0.
panels.title: Planner Tool Calls and Answer Size

panels.description: The rows that the Service ran in the last hour, by lane and result. A result of stopped is a row that the stop of the Service ended, and it is no failure.
panels.title: Service Rounds by Lane and Result

panels.description: The rows that failed in the last hour. The alert RoadmapServiceJobsFailing fires for a row of a repository that has failures and no success in the hour.
panels.title: Service Failed Rounds by Repository and Row

panels.description: The seconds of work of each lane in the last hour.
panels.title: Service Round Seconds by Lane

panels.description: The GitHub requests of the Service in the last hour, beside its limit service.github_requests_per_hour. The cluster Jobs do not count in this budget. To see their requests, set the variable Job to devops-cli-job and read the row GitHub API. If the list does not show this value, no Job ended or sent a request in the time range: make the range wider.
panels.title: Service GitHub Budget

panels.description: The times in the last hour that a hold began: the requests of the last hour used the budget, so no round could start. A request that waits for the budget inside a round does not count.
panels.title: Service Budget Holds

panels.description: The seconds since the last round of each lane of each repository started. The alert RoadmapServiceLaneStalled reads the same series.
panels.title: Service Time Since Round Start

panels.description: The repositories that wait for a round, by lane.
panels.title: Service Queue Depth by Lane

panels.description: 1 while a row of a repository failed its limit of rounds in a row and waits for new input, else 0.
panels.title: Service Suspended Rows

panels.description: The count of each time that GitHub refused the identity of the Service, on the current pod. A value above 0 means that the Service is halted. The series starts with the first refusal, so the panel shows no data until then. The alert RoadmapServiceIdentityRefused reads the same value.
panels.title: Service Identity Refusals

panels.description: The triggers that the Service queued in the last hour, by source: poll or webhook.
panels.title: Service Triggers by Source

panels.description: The webhook deliveries of the last hour, by outcome.
panels.title: Service Webhook Deliveries by Outcome

panels.description: The stops of the implement job in the last hour, by failure class.
panels.title: Service Implement Failures by Class

panels.description: The chat commands of the last hour that the webhook router handled, by command and result.
panels.title: Service Chat Commands by Result

panels.description: 1 while the Service could not write a state record (budget, halt or ledger) to its disk, else 0. The record then lives in memory only, and a restart loses it. The alert RoadmapServiceStateUnkept needs a value above 0 for 15 minutes.
panels.title: Service Unkept State Records

panels.description: The seconds before a suspended row runs its next probe round, as of its last failed round or check, by repository, row and failure class; 0 when the row has no retry time (#4065). The alert RoadmapServiceRowSuspended needs the row to stay suspended for 3 hours.
panels.title: Service Retry After Seconds

panels.description: The deliveries of the hooks of each repository that got no 2xx answer in the last 15 minutes, by repository and status code, as GitHub records them and the metrics row reads them every 13 minutes (#5017). A 403 of the Cloudflare edge never gets to the webhook route. The alert RoadmapServiceWebhookDeliveriesFailed fires above 5 for one repository.
panels.title: Service Failed Webhook Deliveries

panels.description: The stage Jobs of the stage row in the last hour, by result: created, existed (a create that got 409), and the end of a Job that ended with no check-in, which the row recovered: evicted, deadline, failed or succeeded (#4559). A Job that checks in at its end counts its own result in devops_cli_roadmap_stage_total.
panels.title: Service Stage Jobs by Result

panels.description: Open items that the alternatives check can take and has no check for, by repository. An item in the retry delay counts. The Service sends the value twice a day, so each query reads the last value of a day. The alert RoadmapServiceAlternativesNotSearching needs a value above 0.
panels.title: Alternatives Unchecked Items

panels.description: Age of the oldest alternatives check among the items that the check can take, by repository. No line while no such item has a check.
panels.title: Alternatives Oldest Check Age

panels.description: Web searches that the tools ran for each check written in the last day, by verdict: the average, and the number of checks. A skip-class check runs none and shows 0 under not-applicable. Approximate, and low for sparse series: increase() needs two samples of a series inside its window, so a series' first sample, and any series seen only once in the window, add nothing. Delta points from one process can arrive out of order, and totals then come out low (#792).
panels.title: Alternatives Searches per Check

panels.description: The share of the attempts of each roadmap job in the last 7 days that ended with the intended result of the job, from the 'roadmap job result' log lines of the Service and of the pods of the stage Jobs (#4845, #4559). A job with fewer than 30 attempts shows no bar: see Job Attempts. A job with 30 attempts or more and no success shows a bar at 0. The 80% rule (docs/roadmap/job-success.md): a job holds 80% when the ratio is 0.80 or more with 30 attempts or more at 3 daily checks in a row.
panels.title: Job Success Ratio (7 d)

targets.expr: ((sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` | success="true" [7d])) or on (roadmap_job) (sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d])) * 0)) / sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d]))) and on (roadmap_job) (sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d])) >= 30)

panels.description: The attempts of each roadmap job in the last 7 days: one 'roadmap job result' log line for each attempt, in the log of the Service or of a stage Job pod (#4845, #4559). Under 30 attempts the ratio is too few to judge.
panels.title: Job Attempts (7 d)

targets.expr: sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d]))

panels.description: The share of the attempts of each roadmap job in the last 7 days that a cut of the infrastructure ended: the model provider, the CI or the cluster, the memory of a pod, or a used budget (#4845). The ratio counts these attempts as failures.
panels.title: Infrastructure Cut Share (7 d)

targets.expr: (sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` | infra="true" [7d])) / sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d]))) or on (roadmap_job) (sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d])) * 0)

panels.description: The 7-day success ratio of each roadmap job at each daily check, with the line at 0.80 (#4845). A day with fewer than 30 attempts in its 7 days still shows its ratio here. A job with attempts and no success shows 0. The 80% rule (docs/roadmap/job-success.md): a job holds 80% when the ratio is 0.80 or more with 30 attempts or more at 3 daily checks in a row.
panels.title: Job Success Ratio by Day (7 d)

targets.expr: ((sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` | success="true" [7d])) or on (roadmap_job) (sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d])) * 0)) / sum by (roadmap_job) (count_over_time({namespace="devops", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"roadmap-service|devops-cli-job", container=~"service|stage"} |= "roadmap job result:" | json message | line_format "{{.message}}" | regexp `^roadmap job result: job=(?P<roadmap_job>\S+) repo=\S+ item=\S+ result=(?P<result>\S+) success=(?P<success>\S+) class=(?P<failure_class>\S+) infra=(?P<infra>\S+)` [7d])))
